semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For any nonnegative integer b and any ordered list of b positive integers e_1 through e_b satisfying that, for every positive integer d, the number of indices i from 1 to b with d dividing e_i is at least the number of indices i from 1 to b with d dividing i, there exist homogeneous elements u_1 through u_b in the weighted graded polynomial ring over the rationals on generators y_1 through y_b, with degree of y_i equal to i, such that each u_i has degree e_i and the ordered list u_1 through u_b is a regular sequence. In the case b equals 0, this is the empty regular sequence in the ring of rational numbers.

if the hypothesis holds, then there exists an ordered list u_1 through u_b in S
each u_i is homogeneous of degree e_i
the list u_1 through u_b is a regular sequence

statement_nl: Let b be a nonnegative integer, and let e_1,...,e_b be an ordered list of b positive integers. Let S := Q[y_1,...,y_b] be the polynomial ring graded by deg(y_i)=i for 1 <= i <= b. Assume that for every positive integer d, one has |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides e_i}| >= |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides i}|. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials u_1,...,u_b in S such that deg(u_i)=e_i for every i and the ordered list u_1,...,u_b is a regular sequence. When b=0, this means the empty regular sequence in S=Q.
